answer: Karst-water provenance attestation. Each agent identity must present a water sample whose dissolved mineral profile was logged at a registered karst spring by a tamper-evident sensor; profiles vary by recharge path and season, so duplicating one is detectable. A glacier-fed audit stream cross-checks sensor timestamps against melt records. Registration requires an onyx-thin physical tag etched with a per-spring code and scanned by that sensor. Cost: one field visit and tag per identity, so N identities need N distinct sites.
